key_terms: A Hive statement that shows the planned stages, scans, filters, joins and aggregations for a query without running it.
Row counts, sizes and column distributions stored for planning. Stale or missing statistics can produce a correct but inefficient plan.
A join in which the small table is loaded into memory on each task so the large table needs no shuffle.
How many rows a join produces. Duplicate keys can multiply rows without any error, so it must be checked independently.
The runtime, such as Tez or a local path, that Hive uses to carry out a plan. Having Tez installed does not prove a query used it.
evidence: Prepared actual Hive4.2.1/JDK21/PostgreSQL project; live SQL, independent Java Thrift, lifecycle, Iceberg and restore observations remain distinct acceptance gates.
